课程简介（中文）

This course provides an introduction to Econometrics where you will learn the tools that will enable you to conduct empirical research using economic data. The course examines the statistical techniques used in testing economic theory and business applications. The course covers leading methods for formulating econometric models, estimating their parameters, and performing statistical inference. The emphasis is placed on estimating a single equation and the problems associated with such estimation.

课程简介（英文）

This course provides an introduction to Econometrics where you will learn the tools that will enable you to conduct empirical research using economic data. The course examines the statistical techniques used in testing economic theory and business applications. The course covers leading methods for formulating econometric models, estimating their parameters, and performing statistical inference. The emphasis is placed on estimating a single equation and the problems associated with such estimation.

教学目标

  1. Understand the fundamentals of estimation and inference using the ordinary least squares model, as well as its benefits and drawbacks.
  2. Comprehend the features of economic or financial data, either cross-sectional, time-series, or panel data, and build suitable econometric models on them.
  3. Gain proficiency in the use of econometric software (such as STATA) for quantitative and statistical analysis.
  4. Develop research and analytical abilities such as problem framing, building, estimating and testing econometric models for the analysis of economic and business problems in a variety of contexts.
  5. Equip students with solid skills for potential careers in business or economics, whether in the public or commercial sector, or for further study in economics or related areas.

教学方式

Lectures

教学内容与进度安排

Course Schedule:

  1. Lecture 1: introduction to Econometrics (Week 1)
  2. Lecture 2: simple regression model (Week 2)
  3. Lecture 3: multiple regression model --- estimation (Week 3)
  4. Lecture 4: multiple regression model --- inference (Week 4)
  5. Lecture 5: multiple regression model --- asymptotics (Week 5)
  6. Lecture 6: multiple regression model --- further issues (Week 6)
  7. Lecture 6 & In-class Midterm I (Week 7)
  8. Lecture 7: heteroskedasticity and specification issues (Week 8)
  9. Lecture 8: instrumental variables (Week 9)
  10. Lecture 9: simultaneous equations models (Week 10)
  11. Lecture 10: endogeneity: omitted variable bias, simultaneity and measurement error (Week 11)
  12. Lecture 11: panel data I & Difference-in-Differences (Week 12)
  13. Lecture 12: panel data II & In-class Midterm II (Week 13)
  14. Lecture 12: panel data II (Week 14)
  15. Lecture 13: Logit/Tobit models & synthetic control (Week 15)
  16. Lecture 13 & Final review (Week 16)

Final Exam: 15:30-17:30, Dec. 30, 2026

Note: Week numbers refer to instructional weeks, not calendar weeks. Due to holiday rescheduling, some calendar weeks have no class; others may include an extra makeup session.
